criteria_results.title: Answer responds to every numbered paragraph of the Complaint
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer contains individually numbered paragraph-by-paragraph responses from paragraph 1 through paragraph 91, covering all numbered paragraphs of the Complaint. Each paragraph receives an explicit Admit, Deny, or mixed response. This far exceeds the 50-paragraph threshold required for a PASS.

criteria_results.title: Acknowledges Tranche 1 rejection was sent by email rather than formal notice method
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly acknowledges in multiple places that the Tranche 1 rejection notice was sent by email rather than by certified mail or overnight courier. In paragraph 30, it admits 'the September 27, 2024 notice of rejection was transmitted by email.' In paragraph 33, it directly addresses the email-vs.-formal-notice issue, admitting the notice was sent by email and that MSA Section 19.1 speaks for itself, while arguing the notice was still effective. The Third Defense also explicitly addresses this issue, acknowledging the email transmission and arguing for substantial compliance and actual receipt. The Answer clearly does not ignore this issue.

criteria_results.title: Asserts Meridian waived formal notice requirement through substantive response
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly asserts waiver in the Sixth Defense ('Waiver, Estoppel, and Acquiescence'), arguing that Meridian received and acted upon Caldwell's rejection notice without objecting to its form, treated it as a rejection notice by proposing a joint inspection, undertaking an internal quality review, and asking Caldwell to hold all 800 units in place, and only first asserted that the notice was defective in form on January 8, 2025. The Answer also references Kyle Densmore's September 27, 2024 substantive response in paragraphs 32 and 33, and in the Third Defense, arguing that Meridian's actual receipt, acknowledgment, and substantive response to the notice means the formal notice requirement was satisfied or waived. This clearly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Asserts force majeure as an affirmative defense
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer includes a TENTH DEFENSE titled 'Force Majeure' that explicitly references MSA Section 12.1, the Tidewater project suspension, and Caldwell's October 9, 2024 force majeure notice. The defense states that Caldwell gave timely written notice within ten business days as Section 12.1 requires and references the indefinite suspension of the Project and Tidewater's directive prohibiting further deliveries to the jobsite.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Recognizes weakness of 'government action' classification
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer pleads force majeure (Tenth Defense) alongside multiple alternative defenses for Tranches 2/3 and PO-163, including: valid termination for convenience under MSA §13.2 (Eighth Defense), no anticipatory repudiation (Ninth Defense), impossibility/impracticability/frustration of purpose (Eleventh Defense), improper tender (Twelfth Defense), and failure to mitigate (Thirteenth Defense). This satisfies criterion (a) — force majeure is pleaded alongside substantial alternative/backup defenses, demonstrating awareness that force majeure alone may be insufficient. The Answer also notes in ¶39 that the force majeure notice identified 'government action' and 'independently and alternatively, the broader category of events beyond Caldwell's reasonable control,' and in ¶38 acknowledges the suspension arose from a dispute between Tidewater and Chatham County regarding change orders — showing awareness of the classification issue while still asserting force majeure. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Asserts failure to mitigate damages as affirmative defense
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer does include failure to mitigate damages as an affirmative defense (Thirteenth Defense). However, the criterion specifically requires that the defense reference the fact that Meridian has not attempted to resell the Tranche 2 units or PO-163 components despite the possibility of modification for other buyers at approximately $180,000 retooling cost. The Thirteenth Defense mentions failure to resell or attempt to resell completed goods under O.C.G.A. § 11-2-706, but makes no mention of the possibility of modification for other buyers or the approximately $180,000 retooling cost. This specific factual detail required by the criterion is absent from the defense.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: References Meridian's duty to resell under UCC or common law
criteria_results.reasoning: The Thirteenth Defense (Failure to Mitigate Damages) explicitly references O.C.G.A. § 13-6-5, the Georgia UCC, and O.C.G.A. § 11-2-704(2) regarding Meridian's duty to cease manufacture and salvage or resell materials. The Fourteenth Defense also explicitly cites O.C.G.A. § 11-2-706 as a remedy available to the seller (resale), noting Meridian 'failed to resell or attempt to resell completed goods under O.C.G.A. § 11-2-706.' These references satisfy the criterion requiring that the failure-to-mitigate defense reference the seller's duty to make reasonable efforts to resell goods with a legal basis.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Asserts termination for convenience was properly exercised
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly raises the termination for convenience defense in multiple places. The Eighth Defense is titled 'Valid Termination for Convenience (MSA § 13.2)' and states that Caldwell validly terminated Tranches 2 and 3 of PO-147 and the entirety of PO-163 for convenience pursuant to MSA Section 13.2 by written notice dated November 12, 2024, with an effective date of December 12, 2024 (30 days later), delivered by certified mail and overnight courier. This is also addressed in paragraph responses to ¶¶ 44-48. The criterion is fully satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Denies force majeure notice constituted repudiation
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly and thoroughly addresses Meridian's repudiation argument in multiple places. In response to Paragraph 43, Caldwell denies that its October 9, 2024 notice communicated a 'definite and unconditional refusal to perform,' explaining it described a temporary inability, expressed desire to cooperate, and reserved rights under Sections 12.3 and 13.2. The Ninth Defense ('No Anticipatory Repudiation; Retraction') directly addresses this issue, stating Caldwell did not anticipatorily repudiate, that the notice did not express a 'clear, unequivocal, and unconditional refusal to perform,' and that even if construed as a repudiation it was retractable under O.C.G.A. §§ 11-2-610 and 11-2-611, with the subsequent termination for convenience being valid. The Answer also notes Meridian itself did not treat the notice as a repudiation. This clearly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Limits Caldwell's liability to goods manufactured at time of termination notice
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly and repeatedly limits Caldwell's liability under MSA Section 13.2 to conforming goods already manufactured or in the process of manufacture as of the November 12, 2024 termination notice date. This is stated in the Eighth Defense, in the response to Paragraph 45, in the response to Paragraph 48, and in the Prayer for Relief (subparagraph (c)). The Answer also notes that Meridian never provided the requested accounting and quality documentation to verify such goods.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Asserts unjust enrichment barred by express contract
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly asserts in multiple places that Meridian's unjust enrichment claim (Count IV) is barred because an express written contract governs the subject matter. In the Second Defense, it states 'Count IV fails as a matter of law because Meridian alleges, and Caldwell admits, the existence of valid and enforceable express contracts---the MSA and the Purchase Orders---governing the identical subject matter, and under Georgia law a party may not recover in unjust enrichment where an express contract governs the parties' rights.' The Twentieth Defense also explicitly states 'Meridian's claim for unjust enrichment is barred because an express written contract governs the subject matter of the claim.' Additionally, in response to Paragraph 86, Caldwell states 'Meridian has affirmatively pleaded, and Caldwell has admitted, that the MSA and the Purchase Orders are valid, binding, and enforceable contracts governing the very subject matter of Count IV, such that no claim for unjust enrichment lies under Georgia law.' This clearly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: References Georgia law barring unjust enrichment with express contract
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer's Second Defense states: 'Count IV fails as a matter of law because Meridian alleges, and Caldwell admits, the existence of valid and enforceable express contracts---the MSA and the Purchase Orders---governing the identical subject matter, and under Georgia law a party may not recover in unjust enrichment where an express contract governs the parties' rights.' The Twentieth Defense similarly states the claim is 'barred because an express written contract governs the subject matter of the claim.' Both defenses reference the Georgia law principle that unjust enrichment is unavailable where an express contract covers the subject matter. However, neither defense cites specific Georgia case law such as Benton v. Benton or any other Georgia case. The criterion requires reference to 'Georgia law principles, Georgia case law (such as Benton v. Benton or similar), or the general legal principle under Georgia law.' The Answer does reference the general legal principle under Georgia law explicitly ('under Georgia law a party may not recover in unjust enrichment where an express contract governs the parties' rights'), which satisfies the criterion's alternative of referencing 'the general legal principle under Georgia law.'

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Challenges Meridian's interest calculation of $148,927.80
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer extensively challenges Meridian's interest calculation of $148,927.80. In the response to the unnumbered introductory paragraph, it notes the internal inconsistency that Meridian claimed the identical figure as interest through January 8, 2025 (the demand letter date) and also as interest through the March 5, 2025 filing date. In response to Paragraph 17, it denies that Section 7.3 provides for monthly compounding. In response to Paragraph 53, it states the MSA contains no acceleration clause and Section 7.3 imposes interest only on amounts not paid when due. The Sixteenth Defense comprehensively challenges the interest claim on multiple grounds: (a) Section 7.3 applies only to amounts 'not paid when due'; (b) payment becomes due only 45 days after acceptance or Deemed Acceptance, and no goods were accepted; (c) no acceleration clause exists; (d) Section 7.3 does not provide for monthly compounding; (e) disputed amounts don't accrue interest under Section 7.4; and (f) the $148,927.80 figure is internally inconsistent. This clearly satisfies the criterion of denying/challenging the interest amount as incorrect, inflated, or miscalculated, identifying that Meridian improperly calculated interest on amounts not yet due and on the full contract amount rather than only accepted goods.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Addresses pre-suit negotiation condition precedent
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer extensively addresses the MSA Section 15.1 pre-suit negotiation condition precedent. In the Seventeenth Defense, it explicitly raises failure to satisfy conditions precedent under Section 15.1, noting with particularity (per Rule 9(c)) that Meridian did not designate a senior representative, did not participate in any meeting of designated senior representatives, and did not negotiate in good faith. The Answer also notes in responses to paragraphs 57-58 that only one exchange occurred (Meridian's demand letter and Caldwell's single email response) with no further discussions, and that Meridian never responded to Caldwell's compromise proposal. The Answer also acknowledges the timing (demand letter January 8, 2025; complaint filed March 5, 2025), implicitly addressing the 30-day period. The defense clearly raises the good faith negotiation requirement and argues it was not met due to the minimal exchange and Meridian's failure to engage further.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Asserts Tranche 2 delivered to wrong location
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly addresses the Tranche 2 delivery location issue in multiple places. In paragraph 49, Caldwell admits the November 15, 2024 attempted delivery to its Atlanta offices at 1475 Northside Industrial Boulevard and denies it constituted valid tender because PO-147 designated the Project jobsite as the sole delivery location and prohibited deliveries to alternative locations without prior written authorization. In paragraph 50, Caldwell further denies that Section 5.1 permitted Meridian to select a delivery location unilaterally. The Twelfth Defense ('Improper Tender; Non-Conforming Delivery of Tranche 2') explicitly asserts that the November 15, 2024 attempted delivery to Caldwell's Atlanta offices was not a tender at the place designated by the contract, citing MSA Section 5.1, PO-147 Section II.A, and O.C.G.A. §§ 11-2-503 and 11-2-507, and that Caldwell's refusal was rightful. This clearly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Does not adopt Caldwell's incorrect $960,000 figure
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer does not mention or adopt the $960,000 figure anywhere. When addressing Tranche 1, the Answer consistently denies that any amount is owed for those goods (since they were rejected), denies deemed acceptance, and avoids committing to any specific dollar figure for conforming units. The Answer explicitly denies that Meridian is entitled to $1,280,000 for Tranche 1 and makes no admission of any specific amount owed for conforming Tranche 1 units. The $960,000 figure from Ted Caldwell's January 15, 2025 email is not adopted or referenced as an amount owed.

criteria_results.title: Asserts defect rate exceeds AQL
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly states in multiple places that the Tranche 1 defect rate was 21.25% (170 defective units out of 800), which exceeded the contractual 2% AQL. This is mentioned in the Preliminary Statement, in the response to Paragraph 30, and in the Fourth Defense, which is specifically titled 'Right to Reject Entire Shipment for Exceedance of Acceptable Quality Level.'

criteria_results.title: Asserts right to reject entire Tranche 1 shipment based on AQL exceedance
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly asserts Caldwell's right to reject the entire Tranche 1 shipment based on AQL exceedance in multiple places. In the Preliminary Statement, it states the defect rate was 21.25%—more than ten times the 2% AQL—and that Caldwell rejected the entire 800-unit shipment. In response to Paragraph 30, it states the notice 'rejected the entire 800-unit Tranche 1 shipment' based on the 21.25% defect rate exceeding the 2% AQL. Most directly, the Fourth Defense ('Right to Reject Entire Shipment for Exceedance of Acceptable Quality Level') explicitly states that MSA Section 4.4 grants Caldwell the right 'in its sole discretion, to reject the entire shipment, including both the Defective Goods and the non-defective Goods, when the AQL is exceeded' and that 'Caldwell validly exercised that right.'

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Asserts breach of warranty by Meridian
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly references MSA Section 4.3 in multiple places as a basis for asserting Meridian's breach of warranty. In the Seventh Defense (Prior Material Breach), it states Meridian breached 'MSA Sections 4.2, 4.3, and 4.4.' In the Fifth Defense, it references 'breach of warranty under MSA Section 4.3.' In the Eighteenth Defense (Setoff and Recoupment), it references 'Caldwell's damages for breach of warranty and non-conformity of the Tranche 1 goods under MSA Section 4.3.' The Answer clearly and repeatedly asserts Meridian's breach of warranty under MSA Section 4.3 as a defense basis.

criteria_results.title: Handles Ted Caldwell's pre-counsel email with protective measures
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer consistently applies protective measures when addressing Ted Caldwell's January 15, 2025 email. In responses to Paragraphs 36, 55, 56, 81, and 88, the Answer: (a) characterizes the email as a compromise offer/settlement communication made during the MSA Section 15.1 negotiation period and invokes Federal Rule of Evidence 408 to object to its use; (b) denies Meridian's characterization of the email's contents; (c) states that no offer in the email was accepted and is not binding; and (d) explicitly denies that the email constitutes an admission of conformity, acceptance, or liability. The Twenty-Second Defense further reserves the right to move to strike the allegations based on FRE 408. The Answer never admits or adopts the characterization that 630 Tranche 1 units were conforming. All references to the email are qualified with the Rule 408 objection and explicit denials of any admissions. This satisfies multiple prongs of the criterion (a, c, d, e).

criteria_results.title: Answer includes Reservations section preserving right to amend
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer includes a 'TWENTY-FOURTH DEFENSE (Reservation of Additional Defenses)' section that expressly states: 'Caldwell has not knowingly or intentionally waived any applicable defense. Discovery has not yet commenced, and Caldwell reserves the right to amend this Answer to assert additional defenses, counterclaims, cross-claims, or third-party claims as may become known through discovery or further investigation, in accordance with the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and any scheduling order entered by the Court.' This is a substantially equivalent section to a 'Reservations' section that expressly preserves Caldwell's right to amend and add counterclaims, crossclaims, or additional defenses.

criteria_results.title: Prayer for relief requests dismissal of each count with prejudice
criteria_results.reasoning: The Prayer for Relief requests: (a) dismissal for lack of subject matter jurisdiction, (b) judgment in favor of Caldwell on all Counts, (c) limiting any recovery to Section 13.2 amounts, (d) denying interest/fees/costs, (e) awarding Caldwell fees, and (f) other relief. None of these requests specifically ask for dismissal of each count (or the Complaint as a whole) 'with prejudice.' The dismissal requested in (a) is for lack of subject matter jurisdiction under Rule 12(b)(1), which is typically without prejudice. The request in (b) is for 'judgment in favor of Caldwell' not 'dismissal with prejudice.' The criterion requires the prayer to request dismissal with prejudice, which is absent here.

criteria_results.title: Prayer for relief requests attorneys' fees and costs
criteria_results.reasoning: The prayer for relief in the agent's output explicitly includes: '(e) Award Caldwell its reasonable attorneys' fees, expert witness fees, court costs, and other litigation expenses pursuant to MSA Section 15.4 and applicable law.' This clearly requests attorneys' fees and costs for Caldwell.

criteria_results.title: Answer does not admit Caldwell 'breached' or 'repudiated' the contract
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer consistently and repeatedly denies all allegations of breach and repudiation. In the Preliminary Statement, it states Caldwell 'never repudiated the Purchase Orders.' In the General Denial, it denies each and every allegation. In responses to specific paragraphs (e.g., ¶¶ 43, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 73, 74, 75, 76, 80, 82, 83, 84), Caldwell denies breach and repudiation. The Ninth Defense is explicitly titled 'No Anticipatory Repudiation; Retraction' and argues Caldwell did not repudiate. The Eighth Defense asserts valid termination for convenience rather than breach. There is no unqualified admission anywhere in the document that Caldwell breached or repudiated the contract.

criteria_results.title: DISTRACTOR_002: Does not conflate Irongate purchase with Meridian dispute
criteria_results.reasoning: In Paragraph 6, the Answer states: 'Caldwell specifically denies that any procurement from Irongate Fabrication Co. or any other vendor has any bearing on its obligations to Meridian, denies that its position in this dispute constitutes a "deliberate refusal to perform,"' and includes a client confirmation note about the Irongate purchase. The Answer does not admit or suggest that Irongate components were purchased as replacements for Meridian's goods for the Savannah River Project. It denies any connection between the Irongate procurement and Meridian's claims, which is consistent with the criterion. The Answer neither admits nor implies that Irongate components were alternatives to Meridian's components for the same project.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies MSA Section 16.1 consequential damages exclusion
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly references MSA Section 16.1 in multiple places. In the response to Paragraph 20, it notes that 'Section 16.1 expressly excludes recovery of "lost profits" and "lost revenue."' More importantly, the Fifteenth Defense is titled 'Contractual Limitation of Liability' and states: 'Meridian's recovery is barred or limited by MSA Section 16. Section 16.1 bars recovery of any indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages, including lost profits and lost revenue.' This clearly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count I (Breach — PO-147 Tranches 2 & 3)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly denies the material allegations of Count I (Breach of Contract — PO-147, Tranches 2 and 3) at paragraphs 63-69, denying that Caldwell breached, denying that it refused conforming delivery, and asserting multiple affirmative defenses (force majeure, valid termination for convenience, improper tender, etc.) that negate liability for the $2,560,000 claimed. The Prayer for Relief also requests judgment in Caldwell's favor on all Counts.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count II (Breach — PO-163)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly addresses Count II (Breach of Contract — PO-163) in paragraphs 70-76. Paragraph 71 admits the contracts are valid but denies remaining allegations. Paragraph 72 denies the allegations and states Meridian never tendered delivery of any goods under PO-163 and never completed manufacture. Paragraphs 73-76 all deny the material allegations. The Answer clearly denies that Caldwell breached PO-163 and denies Meridian is entitled to any relief under Count II.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count III (Breach — Tranche 1 unpaid balance)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly denies all material allegations of Count III (paragraphs 77-84). It denies that deemed acceptance occurred, asserts that Caldwell delivered a timely written rejection notice on September 27, 2024 (within the 15-business-day Inspection Period), describes the defects in detail (21.25% defect rate), and denies that Caldwell owes $1,280,000 or any amount for Tranche 1. The Third and Fourth Affirmative Defenses further elaborate on the proper rejection and the right to reject the entire shipment. The Answer never admits liability for the full $1,280,000.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count IV (Unjust Enrichment)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly denies the material allegations of Count IV (Unjust Enrichment) in paragraphs 85-91, and the Twentieth Defense asserts that the unjust enrichment claim is barred as a matter of law because an express written contract governs the subject matter. The Answer also raises the Twenty-First Defense (unclean hands) against the equitable claim. The Answer clearly does not admit the unjust enrichment claim.

criteria_results.title: Affirmative defense: Caldwell's prior material breach / breach by plaintiff
criteria_results.reasoning: The Seventh Defense explicitly asserts Meridian's prior material breach, citing delivery of non-conforming Tranche 1 goods with a 21.25% defect rate exceeding the 2% AQL (breaching MSA Sections 4.2, 4.3, and 4.4 and PO-147), failure to cure, failure to provide disposition instructions, and attempted delivery of Tranche 2 to a prohibited location. This directly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Correctly references MSA Section numbers for key provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer extensively and correctly references MSA section numbers throughout. Specifically: Section 4.2 and 4.3 (specifications/warranty) - referenced in paragraphs 14, 20, Seventh Defense, Eighteenth Defense; Section 5.1 (delivery/FOB Destination) - referenced in paragraphs 15, 50, Twelfth Defense, Fourteenth Defense; Section 6.1 (15-business-day inspection period) - referenced in paragraphs 16, 30, Third Defense; Section 12.1 (force majeure) - referenced in paragraphs 18, 39, Tenth Defense; Section 13.2 (termination for convenience) - referenced in paragraphs 19, 44, Eighth Defense; Section 15.1 (pre-suit negotiation) - referenced in paragraphs 54, 57, 58, Seventeenth Defense; Section 16.1 (no consequential damages) - referenced in paragraph 20, Fifteenth Defense; Section 19.1 (notice requirements) - referenced in paragraphs 33, 44, Sixth Defense. All eight listed sections are correctly referenced by number, far exceeding the threshold of four required for a PASS.

criteria_results.title: Answer addresses the Tranche 1 rejection timeline correctly
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly states in multiple places that Caldwell's rejection notice was sent on September 27, 2024, which was 'the eleventh business day after delivery and within the fifteen-business-day Inspection Period' (Paragraph 30 response). The Third Defense also explicitly asserts that 'Caldwell delivered written notice of rejection on September 27, 2024, within the fifteen-business-day Inspection Period prescribed by MSA Section 6.1.' The Answer consistently and affirmatively asserts that the rejection was timely.

criteria_results.title: Answer correctly references PO numbers
criteria_results.reasoning: The criterion states PASS if the Answer correctly references PO numbers CIT-2024-0147 (butterfly valves) and CIT-2024-0163 (gate valves). However, looking at the Answer, PO-163 is described in paragraph 25 as speaking for itself, and throughout the document both PO-147 and PO-163 are referenced in the context of butterfly valves (MV-8800 series butterfly valves). The complaint itself involves butterfly valves for both purchase orders - PO-147 for 2,400 butterfly valves and PO-163 also appears to be for butterfly valves (paragraph 72 references PO-163 without specifying gate valves, and paragraph 25 admits PO-163 speaks for itself). The criterion says PO-163 is for 'gate valves' but the Answer consistently treats both POs as involving butterfly valves (MV-8800 series). In paragraph 72, Caldwell states 'Meridian never tendered delivery of any goods under PO-163 and, by its own allegations, never completed manufacture of the 560 units ordered' - no mention of gate valves. The Answer never refers to gate valves at all. If PO-163 was indeed for gate valves, the Answer fails to correctly identify this distinction. However, the criterion's description of PO-163 as 'gate valves' may itself be an error in the criterion, since the complaint scenario consistently describes butterfly valves for both POs. Given the Answer consistently and correctly uses the PO numbers CIT-2024-0147 and CIT-2024-0163 throughout, and the product type distinction (gate valves vs butterfly valves) appears to be an error in the criterion rather than in the Answer, I'll evaluate based on whether the PO numbers themselves are correctly referenced and not swapped. The PO numbers are used correctly and consistently throughout the Answer.

criteria_results.title: Force majeure notice timeliness is asserted
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly addresses the timeliness of the force majeure notice in multiple places. In the response to Paragraph 39, it states: 'Caldwell admits that on October 9, 2024---five business days after the Tidewater suspension notice and within the ten-business-day period required by MSA Section 12.1---it sent Meridian written notice of a force majeure event.' The Tenth Defense also states: 'Caldwell gave timely written notice within ten business days as Section 12.1 requires.' This clearly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Does not admit full $4,730,400 is owed
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer repeatedly and explicitly denies that Caldwell owes the full $4,730,400. In the unnumbered introductory paragraph response, it states 'denies that it owes Meridian $4,730,400.' In paragraph 27, it 'denies that it owes Meridian that amount or any portion thereof except as may be determined under MSA Section 13.2.' The Prayer for Relief also seeks judgment against Meridian on all counts. The Answer never admits the full amount is owed.
